subject: SLO / monitoring questionnaire for procurement review
messages:

Subject: SLO / monitoring questionnaire for Redwood procurement

Rishi,

Appreciate the time on the call last week. Our procurement and ops teams need concise, traceable answers for how Redwood defines and measures SLOs so we can finish our vendor packet. We've attached a short questionnaire (SLO_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx) and would like a completed version plus a few clarifying notes.

Specifically we need:
- Clear definitions: what counts as a successful inference request, how you compute p95/p99, and how scheduled maintenance is handled in calculations.
- Measurement cadence: rolling vs fixed windows, sampling policy, aggregation frequency (per-minute, per-hour, etc.).
- Storage and retention: where metrics/traces live, retention periods, encryption and cross-region considerations.
- Alerting & escalation: thresholds that trigger pager alerts, escalation flow, and how customers are notified.
- Customer observability: what dashboards or exports customers can access (granularity, per-model or per-route, RBAC).
- Temporary exceptions: process and expected timelines for carveouts.

Can you populate the attached spreadsheet and provide a short one-page summary by EOD Wednesday? Our legal/procurement team will include this in the supplier review.

Thanks,
Jill Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Systems

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLO / monitoring questionnaire for Redwood procurement

Hi Jill —

Thanks for the list. I've completed the spreadsheet first-pass and included explanation notes below; Marissa and Neha are on-copy for any operational or security specifics you need finalized. Summary highlights: 

1) SLO definitions (concise):
- Request success: HTTP 2xx/3xx responses with non-empty body that pass service-level validation (schema and size checks). Client-level retries and malformed requests are excluded.
- Uptime SLO: measured as percentage of successful requests over a 30-day rolling window.
- Latency SLOs: p95 and p99 computed on server-side end-to-end latency (ingress timestamp -> final token emitted). Latency windows are calculated from per-request histograms.

2) Measurement & cadence:
- We capture metrics at 100% for production inference endpoints; no sampling by default.
- Metrics are bucketed per-minute as Prometheus-style time series and rolled up to hourly/daily aggregates for reporting.
- p95/p99 are derived from per-minute histograms using quantile approximation and recomputed on rolling windows (30d/7d/1d).

3) Telemetry storage & retention:
- Short-term metrics: hot cluster stored for 90 days; long-term aggregated histograms and summarized metrics retained 365 days.
- Traces (Jaeger): retained 90 days by default.
- All telemetry encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). For Private deployments we can comply with customer residency rules and KMS/HSM key control.

4) Alerting & incident flow:
- Thresholds: primary paging for SLO breaches uses rolling-window rules (e.g., 30m error-rate spike > 0.5% or p99 latency > contract threshold).
- On-call: SRE on-call rotates; initial page to SRE PagerDuty escalation policy, then product/reliability leads as needed.
- Customers: incidents posted on a public or customer-specific status page; Dedicated/Private customers can receive webhook/PagerDuty/SNS notifications and subscribe to updates.

5) Customer access to metrics:
- Read-only Grafana dashboards with per-customer and per-model panels (latency heatmaps, success rates, request rates).
- For Dedicated customers we provide a streaming metrics feed and CSV exports; role-based access enforced via SSO (SAML/OIDC).
- Time-limited read-only links can be issued for procurement/legal review.

6) Temporary SLO exceptions:
- Submit formal exception request with window and rationale. SRE reviews within 48 hours; if approved we record a carveout with owner and expiration. Extensions require Reliability manager sign-off; contractual changes require legal. Typical operational exception turnaround: 48–72 hours.

Attachments (stubs): SLO_Questionnaire_v3_completed.xlsx; redwood-grafana-sample-dashboard.png. I've also left notes in the spreadsheet where we need procurement to indicate which rows are intended to be contractual vs informational.

Happy to join a short walkthrough with Marissa to demonstrate the dashboard.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Reliability & Production Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-03T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLO / monitoring questionnaire for Redwood procurement

Jill — quick clarifications from Reliability so your ops reviewers have the right expectations: 

- Maintenance windows: scheduled maintenance is excluded from uptime calculations provided we publish the window with >=72 hours notice and annotate the status page. Emergency maintenance is excluded only if declared and recorded by Ops with incident annotations.

- Canary & fallback behavior: for Dedicated customers we can configure progressive rollouts and automatic fallbacks to smaller model variants to preserve latency SLOs; this is configurable in the Dedicated contract and operational runbook.

- Per-route granularity: we can provide per-model and per-API-route SLO matrices. Typical granularity in our deployments: (model, route, region). If you give a list of critical routes we will prioritize those rows as contractual.

I can produce a single-row CSV example showing the fields legal wants (route, success definition, p95/p99 thresholds, measurement window, dashboard link).

—Marissa
Senior Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference

2) We need a redacted incident write-up for a past SLO breach (p99 spike) to show your post-incident annotation style. If you can also share a time-limited read-only Grafana link that procurement can view, that would be ideal.

If you can send these by next Friday that's sufficient.

Jill

- redwood-grafana-sample-dashboard.png (png, 240KB) — screenshot for legal.

Temporary SLO exception process (operational summary):
1) Customer or procurement opens an exception request form with intended window and impact.
2) SRE triages within 48 hours and either approves temporary carveout (adds to exception register with owner and expiry) or requests mitigation.
3) If an extension is needed beyond the approved window, Reliability manager sign-off is required; for contract-level changes legal sign-off is required.

If Acme would like a live 20–30 minute demo of the dashboard and the incident write-up, Marissa and I can run that next week.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
